surfaces_ready dynamically computed via sum(1 for s if READY), not hardcoded
all_mutations_false dynamically computed per-scenario in F37, not hardcoded

Word-boundary regex re.search(r'\b' + ...) correctly used in F37 and test suites (not substring match)

findings.title: _BOUNDARY truncated to 4 flags for legacy routes
findings.description: _BOUNDARY at module level in periphery_ops.py contains only 4 of 15 boundary flags. Used exclusively by pre-F32 pipeline/governance routes, NOT by F33/F36/F38 Brody V1 routes. V1 routes call their respective modules which return full 15-flag BOUNDARY dicts.
findings.risk: Callers of legacy routes receive understated boundary contract. No V1 route affected.
findings.proposed_correction: Expand _BOUNDARY to 15 flags or deprecate legacy routes in F50+

findings.title: safe_backend_response() does not sanitize controlled_response.text
findings.description: strip_forbidden_tokens() is applied only to top-level 'response' and 'response_text' fields. The nested controlled_response.text field returned by F36 and F38 routes is NOT sanitized at the route layer. Defense relies on static template text (F36) and module-level scan (F37).
findings.risk: Single-layer defense for controlled_response.text. If a future module generates dynamic text in this field, route-level sanitizer will not catch it.
findings.proposed_correction: Extend safe_backend_response() to recursively sanitize controlled_response.text and any nested string fields containing generated text

findings.title: surfaces_ready=7 is environment-dependent; docs state as fixed
findings.description: surfaces_ready is dynamically computed. Value of 7 is the nominal result when all upstream dependencies are available. Documentation presents '7 surfaces' as a fixed architectural property without the 'nominal configuration' qualifier.
findings.risk: Demo claims cannot be reproduced in degraded environments. Not a hardcoding issue but a documentation precision gap.
findings.proposed_correction: Add qualifier to all '7 surfaces' documentation: 'nominal configuration; degrades gracefully if upstream unavailable'

findings.title: base.update(data) allows data to override sovereignty base flags
findings.description: In safe_backend_response(), the merge order is base.update(data), meaning data keys override base sovereignty flags. If a backend module returned {allowed_to_decide: True}, safe_backend_response() would propagate that value. The function is a convenience merger, not a sovereignty enforcement net.
findings.risk: Architectural: safe_backend_response() is not a true safety net against a compromised or buggy module. Actual safety guarantee comes from BOUNDARY constant in each module. For V1, all modules are correct.
findings.proposed_correction: Change merge order to data.update(base) so base flags always win, making safe_backend_response() a genuine sovereignty enforcement layer

findings.title: Forbidden token scan scope narrower than some documentation implies
findings.description: FORBIDDEN_RESPONSE_TOKENS is declared in F36 but the module does not call _has_forbidden_token() on its own output. F37 layer actively scans. safe_response.py uses narrow French emission-pattern regex only. F43 runbook states 'word-boundary regex on all generated text' which is accurate for F37+tests but overstates F36 standalone and safe_response layers.
findings.risk: Documentation precision gap. F36 standalone forbidden-token enforcement relies on static template analysis, not runtime scan.
findings.proposed_correction: Add _has_forbidden_token() call to F36 _build_controlled_response() output path, or amend documentation to specify enforcement locus precisely

findings.title: KERNEL_TRACE stdout contains forbidden token strings internally
findings.description: Internal KERNEL_TRACE logging emits stdout lines containing ALLOW, VERDICT, GATE, BLOCK as internal computation traces (e.g., [KERNEL_TRACE] decision=ALLOW sigma=0.73). These are NOT API response tokens. Distinction not documented in boundary contract.
findings.risk: A log scraper or monitoring system treating stdout as audit evidence could flag these as boundary violations. No API response is affected.
findings.proposed_correction: Add explicit note to BOUNDARY contract: KERNEL_TRACE stdout tokens are internal computation results, not API response emissions. Boundary token scan scope = API response payloads only.

findings.title: Hardcoded proof_links in workbench/runtime-connector
findings.description: The workbench/runtime-connector route returns hardcoded proof_links referencing specific F34B timestamp filenames. If proof files are regenerated with new timestamps, links point to stale paths.
findings.risk: Maintenance debt. Files exist for V1. Not a correctness issue within V1 scope.
findings.proposed_correction: Generate proof_links dynamically by scanning docs/runtime/ for files matching F3*_*_PROOF_*.json, or annotate as static V1 snapshot
